_README: Acknowledged drift for the per-subsystem security audits, checked by
frontend/scripts/check-audit-freshness.mjs (runs in `npm run check`).
An audit's `Audited commit` is the code state its claims were verified
against. When the content under that audit's `Code paths` moves away from
it, the check goes red. Two ways out, both legitimate:
1. Re-verify the audit -> bump `Audited commit` in the doc, add a change
log entry, and drop the audit's entry from this file.
2. Review the drift and conclude it cannot move a verdict -> record the
current object id of each `Code paths` entry in `reviewedTrees`, and
append a dated record to `acknowledgements` saying why.
What is NOT legitimate is recording an object id without reading the diff.
The record is the evidence that someone did.
`reviewedTrees` holds git object ids (a tree for a directory, a blob for a
file), not commit SHAs. Get them from the check itself: when it fails it
prints the current id of every path that moved, ready to paste.
Object ids rather than commit SHAs because this repo squash-merges: a commit
SHA written during a PR stops existing when the PR lands, which used to cost
a follow-up commit per acknowledgement. Squashing rewrites history, not
content, so an object id survives it, along with rebases, cherry-picks and
force pushes.
`acknowledgements` is an ordered list of `{ date, note }`, oldest first, and
it is what bounds route 2. Option 2 used to be unbounded: one note string
that only ever grew, so the honest way out stayed available forever and the
audit itself was never read again. Two caps now end that run and force
route 1, whichever comes first:
- 8 acknowledgements. Each one judges its own delta in isolation; the
union of eight of them is not something a ninth reviewer can hold in
their head, and it is the union that decides whether a verdict moved.
- 90 days from the OLDEST record. Drift acknowledged in spring is being
defended by a judgement nobody has revisited.
Both clocks reset the same way: re-verify the audit, bump `Audited commit`,
and delete the entry from this file.

acknowledgements.note: Ctrl+P handed from the webview to the app, read against section 1. No sentence of this audit names it; verdict stays PASS. One path moved and the whole diff is webview_defaults.rs: VK_P leaves the list of accelerators kept with the browser, because globalShortcuts.ts now binds Ctrl+P to printing the open message, and the doc comment and two tests follow. Nothing else in frontend/src-tauri/src changed -- lib.rs, tray.rs, update_preference.rs, the three updater commands, PendingUpdate, DownloadedUpdate and beta_endpoint_override are byte-identical to a2e6d43, generate_handler! exposes the same eight commands, and capabilities/, tauri.conf.json, updates.ts, AboutSettings.svelte and windows-signed-release.yml are untouched. lib.rs also moves one assertion on WEBVIEW_DISK_CACHE_BYTES out of a test into a const assertion beside the constant, which changes no value and no argument the webview is built with, and the webview_defaults.rs doc comment gains a blank line; both are clippy cleanups with no behaviour in them. The handler this edits is attached to the webview controller in setup and is unreachable from the renderer, so section 1's IPC surface is unchanged; the key it stops keeping is a browser accelerator, which no updater path reads.

A doc comment, and nothing else. Verified the way the claim demands rather than by reading the intent: every added and removed line under this path that is neither a `///` line nor blank comes back empty. The paragraph corrected is the one the acknowledgement above introduced -- it said the app now binds Ctrl+P and prints the open message, while printCurrentView calls window.print() and is documented as printing the current view on purpose, so the next reader deciding whether a key may be denied at the WebView2 level was reasoning from behaviour the app does not have. keeps_browser_handling, is_removed_context_menu_item, attach_accelerator_keys, attach_context_menu and their tests are byte-identical, and lib.rs, tray.rs, update_preference.rs, the updater commands and generate_handler! are untouched, as are capabilities/, tauri.conf.json, updates.ts, AboutSettings.svelte and windows-signed-release.yml. No updater path reads any of it. Verdict stays PASS.

Print leaves the WebView2 context menu, read against section 1; no sentence of this audit names the context menu, and the verdict stays PASS. One path moved and the whole diff is webview_defaults.rs. Filtered to lines that are neither comment nor blank, it is exactly two things: is_removed_context_menu_item gains "print" in its matches!, and the test that pins that list is renamed and moves "print" from the kept names to the removed ones. The rest is doc comments saying why: the app now prints only the open message (globalShortcuts.ts), so a context-menu Print would print the folder list or settings page the key refuses to. keeps_browser_handling, attach_accelerator_keys, attach_context_menu and install are byte-identical, and lib.rs, tray.rs, update_preference.rs, the updater commands and generate_handler! are untouched, as are capabilities/, tauri.conf.json, updates.ts, AboutSettings.svelte and windows-signed-release.yml. The handler is attached to the webview controller in setup and is unreachable from the renderer, so section 1's IPC surface is unchanged, and no updater path reads a context-menu entry.

The startup update check's hint is hidden from the accessibility tree, read against section 1; no sentence of this audit names it, and the verdict stays PASS. One path moved and the whole diff is AboutSettings.svelte: the hint paragraph under the checkbox gains aria-hidden="true" and a two-line comment saying why. The checkbox, its checked binding to updateStartupCheck, handleStartupCheckChange and setUpdateStartupCheck, the aria-describedby that still names the paragraph, the update channel select and the Check for updates button are byte-identical, as are frontend/src-tauri/src, capabilities/, tauri.conf.json, updates.ts and windows-signed-release.yml. Nothing the updater reads or writes moved: whether the startup check runs still comes from the registry value through the same two shell commands, and the change is to what a screen reader hears, not to what the control does.

Change under this path, read rather than waved through as a timing tweak. StartupTimingService swapped its reference clock: the anchor for processStartedAt and for every phase's startedAfterProcessMs moved from an Instant.now() taken in the class's own static initialiser to ManagementFactory.getRuntimeMXBean().getStartTime(), with a wall-clock constant recording how much boot had already passed when the class loaded. Section 1 is untouched by it: the diff does not enter StorageContextInitializer, reads or writes no crypto.bin, touches neither the VOXSEC1 format, the DPAPI USER-scope call, the buffer zeroing, the atomic private-permissioned write, nor the constant-time crypto.fingerprint comparison, and adds no path by which any of them could be reached earlier or skipped. The class holds no secret and opens no file. Section 2 holds: CryptoService is not in the diff, and the one place where boot timing and that section intersect - the self-test "warmed off the boot path" claim - is about when the self-test runs, which this change does not move; it only changes what a later dump reports about the time that had already elapsed. The new dependency is java.management, read-only and already in the sidecar's --add-modules list; it is an MXBean read, not a JNI or FFM call, so the "pure Java FFM (no JNI)" hygiene claim of section 1 is about a path this does not join. Section 3 residuals are unaffected - nothing about mail.db plaintext at rest or the same-user-malware exclusion turns on a clock source. The one observable effect outside the boundary is that startup-timings.json in the diagnostic dump now reports a start roughly four seconds earlier and correspondingly larger phase offsets: the same data category as before, no new field and no new value class, and the dump's privacy check is RELEASE_CHECKLIST section 7, which is flagged for a re-take on this candidate for exactly this reason.

A comment, and nothing else: the two changed lines of MailContentService are the comment on the catch around body extraction. It said the wrapped exception lets MailFacade surface a contentError on the cached body; the message detail no longer calls this service and the field is gone, so it now says the caller gets a typed mail error instead of a 500. The sanitize call, the cid collection, the plain-text escape, the byte cap and the oversize flag are byte-identical, and the body still reaches the frame only through /content, which returns what this service produced. Verdict stays PASS.

The exception-text change of API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md 1.9: a new MailFailureCause enum in the exception package classifies a caught exception into a stable cause code, and MailConnectionException / MailOperationException gained constructors that take the cause and pass the classification, not the text, as the message argument. Under this audit's paths only MailContentService changes, in one line: the failure to extract a message's text passes the caught exception as the cause of its MailOperationException instead of appending its text to the message. What the service extracts, sanitizes or renders is unchanged, so no claim of this audit moves.

Every not-found and validation error names a message key of its own, recorded in API_SURFACE_AUDIT.md as v1.11: ResourceNotFoundException(String) and ValidationException(String), which passed the message as the {0} of a generic key, are removed, and each site that used them names a key. Under this audit's path MailContentService changes in two throws: a message missing from the database names error.message.notFound, and one no longer on the server error.message.goneFromServer. What the service extracts, sanitizes, caps or renders is unchanged, so no claim of this audit moves. Verdict stays PASS.

B1-5 fixed again as the 1.53 pass recommended, recorded in the audit itself as v1.54 (section 4e); the fix is this PR's own and waits for an independent pass, so the anchor stays at 4e1b8d7 and this records the drift. Three paths move. Under feature/mail/service only DraftPersistenceService changes: keepTypedRecipients drops the account's drafts beyond its newest KEPT_DRAFTS (1,000), each chain whole, on a save that starts a draft only, and the saved draft's followed revisions beyond its newest KEPT_REVISIONS_PER_DRAFT (100), replacing the account-wide bounds of heads and followed entries; the javadocs that named them follow. DraftRecipientsRepository: deleteDraftsButNewest and deleteRevisionsButNewest replace deleteHeadsButNewest and deleteFollowedButNewest. DraftRecipientsEntity: chain_id is not null, javadocs. The INSERT, the chain lookup, markStored, the forget and the send's lookup by Message-ID are unchanged, so only section 4e's bound moves. Verdict open findings (B1-14, B1-16, B1-17).

B1-17 fixed as the 1.52 pass recommended, recorded in the audit itself as v1.55 (section 4q); the fix is this PR's own and waits for an independent pass, so the anchor stays at 4e1b8d7 and this records the drift. Under feature/mail/service only BoundedImapProtocol changes: DepthBoundedFetchResponse reads an address's mailbox as well as its host, counts the groups started and not ended in the list being read, forgets them with the list as it forgets the group markers, and stops the parse with NestedGroup when a group starts while another is open; parseFetch drops that response with NestedGroupException, a ProtocolException like NestedTooDeepException, and the class javadoc names it. The per-response bounds of B1-3, B1-7 and B1-10, the stalled-parse stop of B1-15, B1-8's command budget and the selection budget of B1-13 and B1-14 are unchanged; the change adds one drop and moves no other claim. Verdict open findings (B1-14, B1-16).

B1-16 fixed as the 1.52 pass recommended, recorded in the audit itself as v1.56 (section 4p); the fix is this PR's own and waits for an independent pass, so the anchor stays at 4e1b8d7 and this records the drift. Under feature/mail/service only BoundedImapProtocol changes: keptBytes charges every body item outside a content fetch as the headers it becomes, through headerBytes and headerBlock, which count the headers as InternetHeaders.load makes them, lines split as LineInputStream splits them; HEADER_LINE_BYTES is new, and the javadocs of keptBytes and DEFAULT_OPEN_FOLDER_BUDGET follow (an ordinary message 9.7 KB rather than 8.8). The refusal is the selection budget's as before, and nothing else moves. Verdict open finding (B1-14).

B1-5 fixed again as the 1.57 pass recommended, recorded in the audit itself as v1.58 (section 4e); the fix is this PR's own and waits for an independent pass, so the anchor stays at 4e1b8d7 and this records the drift. Two paths move. Under feature/mail/service, DraftPersistenceService: saveDraftAsync no longer forgets the replaced revision's entry after its delete, which markStored has already set aside, and forgetTypedRecipients becomes setAsideTypedRecipients, which deleteSupersededDraft calls; SmtpMessageService.sendDraftAsync calls it in place of the forget; javadocs follow. DraftRecipientsRepository: setAside, a plain UPDATE of superseded_at on the named entry when it is not set aside yet, replaces deleteEntry; the javadocs of deleteDraftsButNewest and deleteRevisionsButNewest follow. DraftRecipientsEntity is unchanged. The INSERT, the chain lookup, markStored, both bounds and the send's recipient check are unchanged, so only section 4e moves. Verdict open findings (B1-14, B1-18, B1-19).

B1-18 fixed as the 1.57 pass recommended and wider, recorded in the audit itself as v1.59 (section 4r); the fix is this PR's own and waits for an independent pass, so the anchor stays at 4e1b8d7 and this records the drift. One path moves, feature/mail/service, in three files. ImapAppendService: fetchAndDetachMime charges the draft's header block on the bytes as held (BoundedByteArrayOutputStream.checkHeaderBlock) before the parse and refuses one past MAX_DRAFT_HEADER_BYTES (256 KiB), and returns an UntouchedDraft, a MimeMessage whose saveChanges updates MIME-Version, Date and Message-ID only and leaves the message unmodified, so its content is copied as held and never parsed into parts; javadocs follow. BoundedImapProtocol: headerBytes gains an overload on a byte array, which the ByteArray one now calls; headerBlock, HEADER_LINE_BYTES, keptBytes and every bound are unchanged. SmtpMessageService: a comment by saveChanges. The recipient check, the SMTP send and the Sent append are unchanged, so only section 4r moves, and section 4e's 40 MiB bound with it as the bytes the send holds. Verdict open findings (B1-14, B1-19).

B1-19 fixed, by neither way the 1.57 pass recommended, recorded in the audit itself as v1.60 (section 4s); the fix is this PR's own and waits for an independent pass, so the anchor stays at 4e1b8d7 and this records the drift. One path moves, feature/mail/service. BoundedImapStore overrides both newIMAPFolder forms Angus calls to make a BoundedImapFolder (new), whose newIMAPMessage makes a BoundedImapMessage (new); its handleFetchItem counts with BoundedImapProtocol.headerBlock the header lines of an item Angus would merge (a header item, not all headers asked for, headers already held) and does not hand Angus an item past MAX_MERGED_HEADER_LINES (256) over the message's life; the folder logs one line. Nothing else in the folder or the message changes, and BoundedImapProtocol, every budget and every other bound are unchanged, so only section 4s moves. The folder and message classes now make every folder and message of every IMAP connection, which the whole IT suite, GreenMail and the hostile server alike, ran through green. Verdict open finding (B1-14).

B1-14 fixed again as the 1.52 pass recommended, and wider, recorded in the audit itself as v1.61 (section 4n); the fix is this PR's own and waits for an independent pass, so the anchor stays at 4e1b8d7 and this records the drift. One path moves, feature/mail/service, in one file. BoundedImapProtocol: DepthBoundedFetchResponse counts readNumber and readLong as objects and the characters of every string read (readString, readString(delim), readAtom, readAtomString, the items of readSimpleList) as copiedChars, twice inside an open address group; keptBytes adds COPIED_CHAR_BYTES (2) a character, HEADER_SET_BYTES (1,024) for each charged body item and STRUCTURE_PART_BYTES (1,280) for each part of a BODYSTRUCTURE (structureParts, new); the javadocs of DEFAULT_OPEN_FOLDER_BUDGET and keptBytes are restated for the 1.61 measurements and three connections. headerBytes, headerBlock, the depth, group and stall checks, the budget's value and every other bound are unchanged, so only section 4n moves. Verdict all findings fixed, verification pending.

B1-12 fixed again (IMAP_SMTP_AUDIT.md 1.34, section 4l). Under this audit's paths only AttachmentService changes, inside findPartByPath: a part on the server is asked for its content only when Angus built its parts from the parsed structure (holdsParts), otherwise it is a leaf. Section 4's claims hold unchanged: the part path is validated before any IMAP work, the download streams to a temp file under <data-dir>/tmp that is unlinked on close, and a missing part is a 404 naming the attachment. Verdict stays PASS.

B1-12 regression fixed, recorded in IMAP_SMTP_AUDIT.md as v1.38 (section 4l). AttachmentService.holdsParts recognizes a MultipartDataSource before testing for MimePartDataSource: Angus 2.0.5's IMAPMultipartDataSource extends MimePartDataSource, so the #630 test made every multipart from the server a leaf and its attachments undownloadable. The fall-through over a plain MimePartDataSource is still a leaf; path validation, the temp file and the streaming copy are unchanged. Section 4 of this audit holds unchanged. Verdict stays PASS.

A javadoc in SecurityConfig.pkceAuthorizationRequestResolver now names client_secret_basic, Spring's default for the google registration, where it said client_secret_post (OAUTH_AUDIT.md section 4 note). Comment only: the filter chain, PKCE, CORS and the handlers are unchanged. Verdict unchanged.

B1-5 fixed again, recorded in IMAP_SMTP_AUDIT.md as v1.42 (section 4e). Under this audit's paths only DraftController.saveDraft changes: it calls DraftPersistenceService.acceptDraftSave instead of prepareDraftIdentity, which also writes the typed recipients before the 202, so a database failure there now answers the POST with the generic error instead of failing the async save. The mapping, the path and query validation (@Positive accountId, @Size replaces), the @Valid body bounds and the 202 with its stableId are unchanged, and nothing new is exposed. Verdict unchanged.

B1-14 fixed, recorded in IMAP_SMTP_AUDIT.md as v1.49 (section 4n). Under this audit's paths only application.properties changes: it gains mail.client.imap.open-folder-budget=64MB, a bound on what an open IMAP folder keeps, with its comment. No server, security, CORS, actuator, OpenAPI or other key this audit reads moves, and no endpoint is added or changed. Verdict stays PASS.

A javadoc in SecurityConfig.pkceAuthorizationRequestResolver now names client_secret_basic, Spring's default for the google registration, where it said client_secret_post (OAUTH_AUDIT.md section 4 note). Comment only: the filter chain, PKCE, CORS and the handlers are unchanged. Verdict unchanged.

Two section 4 notes acted on, recorded in the audit itself as v1.6. ExternalProviderLoginService: findOrCreateExternalAccount still looks up (oauth2_provider, external_id) first, then the address, but the address now takes only a row with no oauth2_provider and no external_id (the password upgrade the fallback was written for); a row another identity owns makes the sign-in throw AccountAlreadyExistsException (409, error.account.alreadyExists) before any write, so the row, its binding and its token stay as they are, inside the same transaction that rolls back. markRequiresReauthIfExists takes (providerName, externalId, reason) and finds the account by findByOauth2ProviderAndExternalId instead of findByEmail, and the audit line carries the reason. Under feature/auth only OAuth2LoginService changes: its two callers pass providerName, externalId (validated non-blank by the guard before them) and missing_refresh_token or missing_scope. The four guards, their order, the flag's one clearing path, PKCE, the redirect handling, the session end at /success and the token storage are untouched. What moves narrows what a sign-in may touch: an account another identity owns can no longer be re-bound or flagged by it. Verdict stays PASS.
